stem: A client newly diagnosed with a chronic illness says, 'I don't know how I'm going to live with this.' Which response by the nurse is most therapeutic?

options.A: You will adjust once you get used to the treatment routine.
options.B: Try not to think about the diagnosis until you feel less upset.
options.C: Tell me what concerns you most about how this illness may affect your life.
options.D: You should focus on the positive things and follow the treatment plan closely.

rationale: Therapeutic communication focuses on the client's concerns, uses active listening and open-ended questions, and supports expression of feelings without judgment or unsolicited advice. C invites the client to identify the personal meaning and concerns related to the new diagnosis and allows the nurse to assess coping needs. A provides premature reassurance and predicts an adjustment course. B discourages emotional expression. D gives advice and redirects the conversation away from the client's stated concern.
educational_objective: Use open-ended, nonjudgmental therapeutic communication to help a client express concerns and assess coping after a new chronic-illness diagnosis.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine — NCBI Bookshelf
source_document_title: Nursing: Mental Health and Community Concepts — Therapeutic Communication and the Nurse-Client Relationship
source_locator: Therapeutic Communication: use open-ended questions and active listening to encourage expression and build trust; remain client-centered and nonjudgmental. Working Phase: nurses facilitate awareness of thoughts/feelings and mutually develop individualized goals/coping strategies. Common barriers: giving advice, disapproving tone, and responses that block expression.
source_claim_supported: For a client expressing distress about a new diagnosis, therapeutic nursing communication invites exploration of the client's concerns through open-ended, nonjudgmental listening rather than reassurance, avoidance, or advice.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity: use therapeutic communication; assess client coping and emotional responses to health alterations; provide support that respects individual needs and values.
blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — therapeutic communication and coping with chronic illness
correction_summary: Replaced an abstract recall statement about individualized adjustment with a direct NCLEX-style therapeutic-communication scenario and source-supported response analysis.
audit_findings: NCBI directly supports open-ended, client-centered, nonjudgmental communication and identifies advice/blocking responses as nontherapeutic. C uniquely facilitates assessment and expression; A/B/D are realistic but nontherapeutic. No unsupported grief-stage or fixed-timeline theory remains. Blueprint directly matches Psychosocial Integrity. Independent adversarial second pass found no second answer, cueing, ambiguity or unresolved conflict.
